cmad.notes: No CMAD located. GOES-R is a NOAA-funded operational weather program (NOAA/NASA joint development), not a NASA heliophysics mission subject to the senior-review CMAD requirement, so absence is unremarkable (expected=false). Searched general web for 'GOES-R CMAD' and 'GOES-R Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document' (hits returned only MMS, SDO/EVE, HERMES, SABER, STEREO/SECCHI CMADs), plus goes-r.gov and NOAA NCEI product pages. GOES-R's functional analogues are the Product Definition and Users' Guide (PUG) and per-instrument NCEI calibration/validation reports; these were NOT treated as CMAD front-page (Strong) evidence.

instrument_coverage.notes: Reverse lookup of https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/GOES/16/ returns only two records: MAG and Ephemeris. Both were checked; MAG's ObservatoryID confirms spase://SMWG/Observatory/GOES/16. Ephemeris is a spacecraft-position pseudo-instrument with no science team and was not pursued. The external roster was established from the goes-r.gov instruments page and corroborated by Sullivan's 'GOES-R Series Spacecraft and Instruments' chapter; the two agree exactly. Three of the four space-weather instruments (SUVI, EXIS, SEISS) have NO SPASE Instrument record for GOES-16, so their teams were pursued via provider pages and description references instead of registry Contacts. CCOR flies only on GOES-U and is correctly absent from GOES-16. ABI and GLM are Earth-pointing weather instruments outside heliophysics authorship scope — recorded here for curator completeness, not pursued.

pending_instrument_runs.notes: Description paper located and resolved: Darnel et al. 2022, 'The GOES-R Solar UltraViolet Imager' (Space Weather), 16 authors, not alphabetized; leads 1-3 (Darnel, Seaton, Bethge) taken Strong. A dedicated per-instrument run should register the SUVI record and harvest instrument-team depth (positions 4-16, incl. the Lockheed Martin build team) plus the Vasudevan et al. 2019 SPIE design/on-orbit-calibration paper (10.1117/12.2536196) and the 'GOES-R Series Solar Dynamics' book chapter (10.1016/b978-0-12-814327-8.00018-4, which adds Vicki Hsu).

pending_instrument_runs.notes: Suite-level description reference located and resolved: Machol et al. 2020, 'GOES-R Series Solar X-ray and Ultraviolet Irradiance' (The GOES-R Series, ch. 19), 14 authors, not alphabetized; leads 1-3 (Machol, Eparvier, Viereck) taken Strong. Component runs still owed: EUVS (Eparvier et al. 2009 SPIE, 10.1117/12.826445 — NOTE: partially alphabetized, prefix = Eparvier alone) and XRS (Woods et al. 2024 JGR, 10.1029/2024JA032925 — not alphabetized, leads Woods, Eden, Eparvier). Component leads Woods, Eden, Crotser and Jones are excluded at observatory level as component-instrument depth and should be harvested at Strong/Medium on those component runs.

pending_instrument_runs.reason: no SPASE record + paper-selection uncertain (two co-equal suite-level description references from different communities)
pending_instrument_runs.notes: Two competing suite-level descriptions score similarly on the heuristics: Galica et al. 2016 SPIE (builder team, Assurance Technology Corporation — 'instruments overview, calibration results, and data processing algorithms') and Kress, Rodriguez & Onsager 2020 (NOAA science team, The GOES-R Series ch. 20). Neither dominates, so the self-aware downgrade rule was applied and leads 1-3 of BOTH were taken at Medium rather than Strong. SEISS is itself a suite (MPS-HI, MPS-LO, two SGPS, EHIS + DPU); a dedicated run should register SEISS and its sub-sensors and settle the description-reference question.

notes: Record's own Contacts are effectively empty: a single GeneralContact pointing at spase://SMWG/Person/UNKNOWN — a non-qualifying role AND a placeholder rather than a real person. It yields no candidate. Every candidate below therefore comes from sources outside the record. RevisionHistory names only the metadata editor initials 'JWL' (2026-07-20 SPASE 2.7.1 update), which is metadata curation, not authorship.

SPASE instrument coverage for GOES-16 is thin but not empty: MAG and Ephemeris are registered; SUVI, EXIS and SEISS have no Instrument record. This is better than the sibling GOES-18 record (zero instruments registered) and the MAG record is what recovers Howard J. Singer as PrincipalInvestigator. The three missing space-weather instruments are a metadata gap worth surfacing to curators.
No CMAD exists and none is expected — GOES-R is a NOAA operational program, not a NASA senior-review mission (see the cmad object).

MISSION-OVERVIEW SELECTION (observatory level) is UNCERTAIN and was downgraded one tier. No peer-reviewed heliophysics mission-overview paper exists for GOES-16; the mission's authoritative reference is the edited volume 'The GOES-R Series: A New Generation of Geostationary Environmental Satellites' (Goodman, Schmit, Daniels & Redmon, eds., Elsevier 2020, ISBN 978-0-12-814327-8). Its Introduction (Goodman, sole author) and 'GOES-R Series Spacecraft and Instruments' (Sullivan, sole author) chapters were used as the observatory-level description, so Goodman and Sullivan enter at Medium rather than Strong. Both are single-author chapters, which normally argues against description-paper status — they are accepted here because they are overview chapters of the mission's own reference volume, not stand-alone science papers. Flagged for reviewer judgment.

SUVI description paper (Darnel et al. 2022, 10.1029/2022SW003044): selection CONFIDENT — the title is exactly the instrument name, 16 authors, peer-reviewed (Space Weather), and it is the series-level instrument paper. It sits ~6 years after the GOES-16 operating-span start, slightly outside the nominal 2-5 year window; accepted because the GOES-R series spans 2016-2024 launches, so a 2022 series-level instrument paper is well inside the series era, and the competing candidate (Vasudevan et al. 2019 SPIE) is a builder design/calibration paper, not the instrument description. Backward alphabetization scan: longest sorted suffix = Edwards, Mathur, Timothy (3 names, below the 5-name threshold), so NOT alphabetized; positions 1-3 (Darnel, Seaton, Bethge) taken Strong, positions 4-16 excluded as SUVI instrument-team depth.

MAG description paper (Loto'aniu et al. 2019, 10.1007/s11214-019-0600-3): selection CONFIDENT — titled 'The GOES-16 Spacecraft Science Magnetometer', naming this exact observatory; 15 authors; Space Science Reviews; 2019, three years after the operating-span start. Backward scan: sorted suffix = Chu, Early, Kronenwetter, Todirita (4 names, below threshold), so NOT alphabetized; positions 1-3 (Loto'aniu, Redmon, Califf) taken Strong. Position-4 author Howard J. Singer is included at Medium via an INDEPENDENT source — PrincipalInvestigator in the GOES-16 MAG SPASE record plus the record Acknowledgement — not via paper position, per the symmetric scoping rule.

EXIS description reference (Machol et al. 2020, 10.1016/B978-0-12-814327-8.00019-6, 'GOES-R Series Solar X-ray and Ultraviolet Irradiance', The GOES-R Series ch. 19): selection CONFIDENT at suite level — it is the only description covering BOTH EXIS components (EUVS and XRS), has 14 authors, and appears in the mission's own reference volume four years after the operating-span start. Backward scan: sorted suffix = Bouwer, Reinard (2 names), so NOT alphabetized; positions 1-3 (Machol, Eparvier, Viereck) taken Strong. This supersedes the sibling GOES-18 run's approach, which lacked a suite-level reference, declared EXIS selection uncertain, and harvested the EUVS/XRS component papers instead.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE GOES-18 RUN (flagged for reviewer): (a) The EUVS design paper (Eparvier et al. 2009, 10.1117/12.826445) is PARTIALLY ALPHABETIZED — the backward scan finds a sorted suffix of exactly five (Crotser, Jones, McClintock, Snow, Woods), so the deliberate prefix is Eparvier ALONE. The GOES-18 run treated Crotser (2) and Jones (3) as leads; the alphabetization scan does not support that, and per the skill a short prefix must never be padded from the alphabetized tail. Crotser and Jones are therefore excluded here. (b) Thomas N. Woods and Thomas D. Eden lead the XRS component paper, but XRS is a component of the EXIS payload instrument, so under the Observatory-record scoping rule their lead authorship belongs to the EXIS/XRS component run, not this list; GOES-18 included them at Medium. Both divergences are recorded as excluded candidates with full evidence rather than dropped, so a reviewer can reinstate them if the intended scoping treats EUVS/XRS as top-level instruments.

SEISS description-reference selection is UNCERTAIN — two suite-level descriptions score similarly and come from different communities: Galica et al. 2016 (SPIE; builder team at Assurance Technology Corporation; 'instruments overview, calibration results, and data processing algorithms, and expected on-orbit performance'; 6 authors; 2016, valid pre-launch design/overview per the fuzzy lower boundary) and Kress, Rodriguez & Onsager 2020 (The GOES-R Series ch. 20; NOAA science team; 3 authors). Neither dominates on the heuristics, so the self-aware downgrade rule was applied: leads 1-3 of BOTH were taken at Medium instead of Strong, and Galica's positions 4-6 dropped to Low (excluded). Both author lists are non-alphabetized (Galica: no sorted suffix at the tail; Kress: 3 authors, below threshold).

Instrument roster cross-check: the goes-r.gov instruments page and Sullivan's 'Spacecraft and Instruments' chapter agree exactly on the GOES-16 payload (ABI, GLM, SUVI, EXIS, SEISS, MAG) — no roster conflict. CCOR is correctly absent (GOES-U only).

The GOES-R program team page was read for observatory-level contacts. Daniel T. Lindsey (current GOES-R Program Scientist) holds a qualifying role and is included at Medium; note he is Earth-science/ABI-focused (he authored the ABI RGB-composites chapter), so a reviewer may prefer to scope him out of a heliophysics DOI. Edward Grigsby, Monica Todirita and Steve Bidwell hold management/engineering-management titles that are NOT qualifying roles and are recorded as excluded. The remaining program-office staff on that page (Steve Grippando, Joe Kolesnick, Lili Alvarado, Eli Krall, Sislyn Barrett, Maryann Orellana, Jeremy Wilson) hold budget, procurement, contracting, chief-of-staff and IT-services positions; they were evaluated and are not authorship candidates under any source, so they are not carried as individual entries.

Steven J. Goodman's ProgramScientist tenure is documented as 2007-2017, which spans the GOES-16 build and its 2016-11-19 launch — recorded in activity_dates for the downstream role agent. Daniel T. Lindsey is the current holder of that role, so the two represent successive generations of GOES-R program scientist.

Initials-only names (G. E. Galica, B. K. Dichter, S. Tsui, W. Rowland, S. Macintyre, C. Chastain, R. Dence, R. Bailey, E. Shoemaker, F. J. Rich, D. Chu, D. Early, J. Kronenwetter, M. J. Golightly, C.
